subject: truck2077
pitch:
Category: Vehicle.
Subject: futuristic militarized truck from 2077.
Style: low-poly cyberpunk, extremely intricate.
reasoning:
I'm planning a compact but visually rich truck model using the builder, combining basic geometries, extrusion, lathing, glow effects, and SVG textures with paints. Since it's a static model, I can skip rigging joints for the wheels and keep the structure simple.

I'm working out the truck's dimensions and part layout: an 8m-long chassis with six wheels on three axles, a dark armored cargo body, and a cab built from an extruded sloped-windshield profile defined by a series of (z,y) coordinate points to shape the front end.

Positioning side windows as glowing dark teal boxes, adding a sloped hood with front bumper ram, light bar glow strip, and amber/cyan headlight slits, then building the wheels as rotated cylinders with dark tires and emissive hub rings placed along the axles.

Now I'm adding fenders over the wheels, a roof turret with twin glowing-barrel guns, rocket pods and missile tubes on the cargo roof, plus an antenna array, sensor dish, neon side light strips, underglow, hazard-striped armor panels, a "2077" emblem decal, and a rear door.

I'm planning the remaining textures (hazard stripes, emblem label, windshield HUD, rear door glow) and sketching a helper function for mapping textures onto plane geometry facing a given direction, then setting up paint materials using a panelled mottled gunmetal finish from the clockwork kit.

I'm defining a box-building helper that creates part geometry with position and rotation options, plus mirror loops to duplicate symmetric parts, then moving on to shape the cab hood and add neon side stripe details.

Working out the wheel positions relative to the chassis width and checking that the cab's half-width overlaps the wheel arches correctly so nothing clips awkwardly.

Adjusting the vertical layout: moving the cab and cargo floor up to y=1.3 so wheels tuck under cleanly, adding fender boxes and chassis fill between 0.55 and 1.3, and resizing the cargo box height accordingly while adding side-skirt armor between the wheels.

Placing the turret on the cab roof around z=1.6, setting cargo depth from z=-3.6 to 0.8, and sizing the chassis and bumper to fit within the overall height of about 3.9 units with antennas. I'll now write out the full code with a textured bumper box carrying hazard stripe coloring, then move to meta export.
